model_output.verdict: An experienced math teacher with a clear start in digital learning design, but few details on what changed.
write_up: A recruiter sees a math teacher who teaches advanced courses and is building digital learning experience. The hesitation is that the learning design work is still a small part of the page, with little about how students responded to it.
The Canvas module line is the model: it names the subject, the format and the platform. Give the professional learning community and the video work a little more of that same substance.

cards.line: - Redesigned the Algebra II unit on functions into a self-paced online module in Canvas
cards.cannot_tell: This works because a reader can picture the unit and what you made from it. It's a useful model for the other learning design work.

cards.line: - Lead the math department's professional learning community
cards.cannot_tell: The leadership is yours, but the page doesn't say what the community works on. A topic or deliverable would make the work easier to picture.
cards.example: Lead the math department's professional learning community on [topics], producing [deliverable]
cards.question: What does the community work on, and what has it produced?

cards.line: - Created video walkthroughs that students use for exam review
cards.cannot_tell: Exam review gives the videos a purpose, but their content is still a blank. A topic and any student response you can verify would give the work more weight.
cards.example: Created video walkthroughs on [topics] that students use for exam review; [student response, if known]
cards.question: What topics did the walkthroughs cover, and what do you know about students' response to them?

fit.note: The page fits mathematics teaching most directly. The Canvas module, portfolio and certificate in progress also point toward digital learning design, though that work has less room on the page.
